<ANSWER>1</ANSWER>

The given statements describe direct ancestor-descendant relations, which can be represented as a directed graph where an edge from A to B indicates A is an ancestor of B (i.e., B is a descendant of A). All 63 statements were parsed into these directed relations, and transitive chains were constructed by linking them end-to-end.

Starting from Ashley yields the chain:  
Ashley > Rebecca > Ethan > Kevin > Helen > Theresa > Michael > Sophia > Danielle > Elizabeth > Henry > Eric > Vincent > Lawrence > Alexis > Megan > George > David > Melissa > Gloria > Bryan > Samuel > Emily > Janet > Heather > Richard > Kimberly > Donna > Stephen > Linda > Jack > Ralph > Joan > Sara > Judith > James > Jacqueline > Paul > Philip > Juan > Emma > Thomas > Denise > Karen > Sean > Nicole > Maria > Adam > Kenneth > Andrea > Mark > Kathleen > Roy > Anthony > Jeffrey > Evelyn > Joyce > Michelle > Charles > Debra > Katherine > Patrick > Andrew > Jose.

This chain incorporates every name exactly once with no branches, cycles, or contradictions (each named relation aligns with its position in the sequence, and no statement places any individual both above and below another in an inconsistent way). Since Ashley appears at the start of the chain and Jose at the end, Ashley is a (distant) ancestor of Jose. This directly matches option 1; the other options are inconsistent with a single linear chain (no shared ancestor or descendant apart from the direct line itself, and Jose cannot be Ashley's ancestor).
